title: Augustana College GIS Student Final Presentations
text:
Presentation
Augustana College GIS Student Final Presentations in December 2026: Locations for both presentations will be:
Swenson Hall of Geoscience, 820 38th St, Rock Island, IL 61201 (free parking along 38th street) Room 210
Drone Mapping & GIS: Monday, December 7th, 3-5pm
Students will present their final drone mapping projects, including how they designed, planned, and conducted a safe, FAA-compliant UAS mission. They will also present their resulting map products and explain how they meet the requirements of a spatial request, with an emphasis on accuracy and image quality.
Cartography: Friday, December 11th, 9-11am
Students will present (5-8 mins each) an original map they designed and created from scratch, using their own ideas and data to communicate a topic of their choosing. Each student will briefly introduce their map, explain its purpose and audience, and highlight design choices they made to achieve our course goal of accurate & effective spatial communication.

title: USACE UAS and GIS Integration
text:
Presentation
Carli Schalbowske 
This presentation will be discussing how to integrate Uncrewed Aerial Systems (UAS) with GIS workflows. It highlights applications used by the United States Army Corps of Engineers, including high-resolution orthomosaic and 3D mesh generation, infrastructure inspection, long-term monitoring and geospatial data collection. The presentation will also cover how UAS-derived datasets can be incorporated into GIS for improved spatial analysis, data accuracy, and more efficient project planning and decision support.

title: Versioned Parcel Fabric Implementation
text:
Presenters: Mick Frus, Cameron Shotton, Andrew Sunderman
The Rock Island District Implemented versioned parcel fabric editing in 2023 to support multi-user editing to the District’s cadastral data. In this month’s meeting, we look to discuss implementation, workflows, and findings since implementing parcel fabric. We’d love to hear from other users on their own methods and best practices for editing and managing cadastral datasets.

section: Bring your ideas and experience to the group.
text:
Bring your ideas and experience to the group.
If you are interested in presenting please email Bobby Oliver at the contact link below. Provide your name, organization, topic of talk, what technology is needed for your presentation, and what is the best month, day and time you’re available.

GIS Certifications
Here is the link to the Geographic Information System Certification Institute (GISCI) for those interest in becoming a GISP.   GISCI Link  


Geospatial Communities

The GPN
The Geospatial Professional Network is a vibrant community uniting emerging and experienced GIS professionals through top-tier education, networking, and career development. We are committed to upholding ethical standards, empowering you to support your organization, advance your career, and shape the future of the geospatial profession.  
The GPN Link   


WiGIS
Women in GIS is an inclusive group of women and allies coming together to provide support, resources, and opportunities for success as you navigate your geospatial career.

WiGIS Link   


ASPRS
The American Society for Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing (ASPRS) is a scientific association serving thousands of professional members around the world. Our mission is to advance knowledge and improve understanding of mapping sciences to promote the responsible applications of photogrammetry, remote sensing, geographic information systems (GIS) and supporting technologies.

ASPRS Link

title: QC-GIS
text:
Quad Cities GIS User Group
Establishing a GIS User Group in the QC area creates a network of partnerships with local organization, educational institutions and all other GIS users. It provides essential professional involvement in our local community, strengthens existing partnerships, and creates access to a pool of local GIS knowledge and resources.

Meetings
Upcoming meeting info is emailed out to the user list prior to the meeting. Please signup for emails at the bottom of this page. The days, times, and locations of the meetings will vary in an attempt to accommodate more people. Meetings are held the 2 week of the months listed in the schedule and at one of the following locations. See the schedule below.

Augustana College, Hanson Bldg, 3520 Seventh Ave, Rock Island, IL 61201 (Room 234). Meeting time from 1-2pm on Fridays
Bi-State Regional Commission, 1504 Third Ave, Rock Island, IL 61201 (Room 201). Meeting time from 12-1pm on Wednesdays

title: Rock Island Common Operating Picture (RCOP)
text: The RCOP is used to support Rock Island Districts Emergency Response reporting and field data collection. She will first provide an introduction to field data collection and then provide a tour of the application suite used to power situational reporting and briefings during an emergency response event. This presentation will focus on how the RCOP is used to respond to flooding within the Rock Island District.  ##

title: Scott County Situational Awareness Dashboard
text:
Breanna Pairrett  
This presentation will be talking about the Situational Awareness dashboard that my colleague and I created in Experience Builder. We use this mostly for our Radiological Evacuation Plan exercises that are graded by FEMA. It was recognized by FEMA two years ago as National Best Practice, then published on ESRI’s Forbes Channel, which led to us being awarded a SAG Award last year at the 2025 ESRI UC. 
It is a multi-use tool that allows us to adapt to any emergency or event. We mostly utilize the Near Me Analysis tool that allows us to get quick insight counts of schools, tier II facilities, govt buildings, parcel information, etc. within a specified area (point, line, polygon) search radius

title: Spatial Ops GIS Programs
text:
Morgan Franck (Anderson)
This presentation gives an overview of GIS in Operations, or the “Spatial Ops” team’s GIS programs, covering their structure, job duties, and data management. It details key activities such as hydrographic surveying, dredging support, the eHydro program, and the creation of navigation charts supporting the USACE Rock Island District’s navigation mission.
